pulse.text: **Google's next Pro model slipped further out**: Polymarket cut the Gemini 3.5 Pro Sep 30 leg to **14%** from 27%, while the Oct 31 leg held at 73% - traders now put the release almost entirely in October or later. The counterweight was OpenAI, where GPT-6's Oct 31 leg jumped to **64%** from 55% and Astra's Sep 15 leg rose to 63%, with DevDay on Sep 29 the obvious catalyst. Nothing shipped: the model board is unchanged since GLM-5.3-Flash and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on Aug 26, and **Claude Opus 5 still leads the AA-Index at 63** over Fable 5 at 62 and GPT-5.6 Sol and Grok 4.6 tied at 61. Anthropic has effectively locked August's best-model market at **99.6%** ahead of Monday's resolution, and holds 94% for September and 70% for year-end. Benchmark optimism cooled a notch - an AI clearing 90% on FrontierMath before 2027 eased to **86%** from 90% - while CNBC reported the public backlash against AI reaching a fever pitch as data-center opposition turns into a midterm campaign issue.
